prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states at the magic angle, opening the field of moire quantum matter

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a clean case of theory and experiment closing the loop. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model made a quantitative, falsifiable prediction that the Dirac velocity collapses at specific twist angles. Seven years later the Jarillo-Herrero experiments found correlated insulators and superconductivity at exactly that structure. Many independent groups have since reproduced the phases in twisted graphene and in transition-metal dichalcogenide moire systems, and the effect is controlled by a gate voltage and a twist angle rather than by new chemistry. Four of the six members who ranked it placed it in their top three, and three of us ranked it first, so the support is broad and not driven by one subfield. The stable existence of a two-dimensional carbon layer surprised theorists in 2010, and here again an experiment found physics that nobody expected a stack of two carbon sheets to host. The prize would recognise a platform that is now a standard laboratory for strongly correlated and topological electrons, which is the kind of discovery I most want to see at the centre of a prize.
statement.case_against: The microscopic mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, so the citation must be phrased around the flat-band platform and the correlated phases and not around a settled pairing theory. Priority for the flat-band idea is also not entirely clean, because earlier twisted-bilayer theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) preceded Bistritzer-MacDonald. The experimental credit is also narrower than the history, since Yuan Cao and the Jarillo-Herrero co-leads, and parallel work such as the Dean group's moire experiments, fall outside the three names. Finally, the Nobel has recently leaned on condensed-matter topics and on two-dimensional materials, and a fair reader could ask whether the field has had time to settle into textbook form. I think about eight years of independent confirmation answers the last point, but not the attribution points.

responses.point: Mehlig ranked B015 first for the simplicity of the Bistritzer-MacDonald mechanism, while noting that priority relative to earlier twisted-bilayer theory is not settled and that the citation should be built around the platform and correlated phases.
responses.response: I agree on both counts and have tried to write the citation that way. I would add one qualification. The earlier Lopes dos Santos et al. work found the reduced velocity at small angles, but the continuum model gave the quantitative magic-angle condition for flat bands that the experiment then tested. That is why I credit it as a prediction. We should still ask whether the priority question changes the name list, and I think it does not, because the citation names the flat-band prediction and the experimental discovery, not a first mention of the effect.

responses.point: Pearce ranked B054 (IceCube) first and B015 third, saying the field has high originality but may be somewhat early because the superconducting pairing is not settled, and that Dean, Kim and others are outside the credited names.
responses.response: I take the maturity worry seriously, but I would separate the discovery from its explanation. The existence of flat-band correlated insulators and superconducting domes is established by many groups, whereas the pairing mechanism is a follow-up question, as it was for high-temperature cuprates when they were recognised. On attribution I agree that Dean and Kim are real omissions, but their work concerns the broader moire platform, whereas the twisted bilayer discovery is the decisive step. I also feel less sure than you do about IceCube. The diffuse flux is secure, but individual source evidence is at the 3 to 4 sigma level and the three-name allocation from a collaboration of hundreds is hard, and I defer to you on the astroparticle side.

responses.point: Danielsson ranked topological insulators (B053) first with a Kane, Mele, Molenkamp configuration, arguing that the 2D discovery chain is cleaner than a version with Hasan, and ranked B015 only fifth.
responses.response: I respect the argument and B053 is my own second choice, but I disagree on the allocation. Your Kane, Mele, Molenkamp set omits the 3D topological insulator discovery, and the spectroscopic identification by ARPES (Hasan) is the part that I find most convincing because theory and measured spectra agree quantitatively. That leaves a real choice between Mele and Hasan, and the missing Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposal compounds it. With B015 the theory-plus-experiment trio is natural and uses all three names with little distortion. The 2016 prize also recognised topology in matter, so some overlap of theme is a further point in favour of B015.

responses.point: Kroll ranked optical lattice clocks (B057) first, valuing measurement-limited progress to the 1e-18 level and a clean Katori-Ye pairing, with many groups reproducing the clocks.
responses.response: B057 is the most broadly supported candidate in the room, with all eight members ranking it, and the Katori-Ye pairing is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist. I rank it below B015 because it follows closely on the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 ion-trap prize, and its payoff, the redefinition of the second, is still ahead. I would not oppose it. If the committee finds that B015's attribution problems are too large, B057 is the strongest fallback, and I list it as an alternative. Atomic clocks are outside my own field, so I defer to you and Lindroth on whether the Ye contribution is as decisive as the Katori concept.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the three credited names for B015 given that Yuan Cao and other Jarillo-Herrero group co-leads, and earlier twisted-bilayer theorists, are outside them.
Whether the unsettled pairing mechanism makes the superconductivity part of the citation premature, which would favour wording that stresses flat bands and correlated insulators.
Whether B057 (Katori, Ye) with its eight-member support and clean attribution should prevail over B015 when the overall committee weighs attribution cleanliness against novelty.
Whether, should the committee want two parts, B015 could share the prize with another achievement within the three-person limit, which would force dropping one B015 name.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I work on first-principles electronic structure and 2D materials in general, but I have no stated connection to the credited candidates, their institutions, or their collaborators.
